svg.aria-label: Diagram: AWS IAM trusted identity propagation extended to IAM federation and IAM Roles Anywhere. TIP attaches identity context from a trusted source when AWS creates a role session, and after AWS attaches the context callers cannot change it during the lifetime of the session. Trusted sources include configured external identity providers for AWS IAM federation and X.509 certificates validated against configured trust anchors for IAM Roles Anywhere. Enabling TIP on an identity provider already in use carries a hard failure mode: a missing required Subject source or a present invalid mapped value causes AWS STS to reject the federation request with InvalidIdentityToken, while an absent optional runtime claim is simply omitted from the session. The propagation boundary is derived by AWS from the account that owns the IAM identity provider and, when that account belongs to an organization, from that organization. Within the boundary AWS STS carries TIP context into a new role session without requiring a customer-authored Allow for sts:SetContext. Outside it, AWS STS drops TIP context at the time of the new role assumption, and the role assumption can still succeed if the applicable IAM permissions and the target role's trust policy allow the request, so access continues while attribution stops. The same boundary behaves differently for a direct request, because a direct request to a resource in an account belonging to another organization uses the original session credentials and does not create another role session, so the context is still carried. When a supported AWS service assumes an IAM service role, AWS STS applies the same boundary and does not use the AWS service principal's account. Limits are one Subject, an optional Subject type, and up to 10 additional values mapped as runtime claims; each key is 1 to 128 characters and each value must be a single value of no more than 128 characters. There is no separate aggregate runtime-claim quota because TIP context shares the capacity of the AWS STS session token with other session data, and an oversized session fails with PackedPolicyTooLarge. For SAML, the Issuer context key is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-384 hash of the DER-encoded public key used to verify the assertion signature, and identifies the signing key rather than the assertion Issuer element. TIP context does not grant permissions. In CloudTrail, core origin identity appears in userIdentity.onBehalfOf and runtime claims in userIdentity.transactionContext.IdentityProvider, while the IAM role remains the AWS principal in the event. AWS recommends not including personally identifying information in the Subject and suggests an opaque immutable identifier, yet group-based access requires the Subject value to match the corresponding user's Username in IAM Identity Center.
svg.title: Turning it on can reject the logins that already work
svg.text: An additive feature with a subtractive failure mode.
“A missing required source or a present invalid mapped value causes AWS STS to reject the federation
request with InvalidIdentityToken.”
Absent is harmless. Present and wrong costs you the login.
claim not sent at all omitted from the session
claim sent, invalid FEDERATION REQUEST FAILS
Empty, whitespace, multi-valued, over 128 chars, or a Subject type that is not user or workload.
The boundary drops the context and lets the call through
origin in an org → same org context CARRIED
origin in an org → other org / solo context DROPPED
origin standalone → any other account context DROPPED
“The role assumption can still succeed.” Access continues; the audit trail stops.
ASSUME VS CALL: OPPOSITE
Assume a role cross-org — context dropped
Call a resource cross-org — context kept
A direct request “does not create another role
session”. Minting credentials is the trigger.
THE LIMITS
Subject exactly one
runtime claims up to 10
key / value 128 chars each
No aggregate quota: it shares the STS session token.
For SAML, Issuer is not the Issuer
“The resulting value identifies the signing key, not the SAML assertion Issuer element.”
A SHA-384 hash of the DER-encoded public key — so it changes when the certificate rotates.
The Subject should be “an opaque, immutable identifier” — and group access needs it to equal the Identity Center Username.
Context is attached only after validation, and a downstream caller cannot change or remove it.
CloudTrail: userIdentity.onBehalfOf and userIdentity.transactionContext.IdentityProvider. The role is still the principal.
TIP context does not grant permissions. Policies and supported services decide how to use it.
